parts.title: The Mango or the Seed: Which Came FIRST? (Part 2) | 3 Stages of a Plant's Life Cycle
parts.description:
An old mango tree is covered in tiny flowers. Which stage is it in? Look closer at our young plant beside the old tree, be a mango flower, find where new seeds come from, and learn the three stages in the life cycle of a plant. Then visit Singapore's seed bank. Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Life Cycles of Plants.

In this part:
• Look closer: a young plant and an adult plant side by side
• Be a mango flower: from flower to fruit, with a seed inside
• The three stages: the seed, the young plant and the adult plant
• Showdown: find the mistake in Momo's homework (no first or last stage!)
• Look closer: Singapore's seed bank
• A chant to remember it all
• Spot the hidden weaver ant!

Key words: adult plant, three stages, seed bank.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: a tadpole. What will it grow into?

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

One mango seed to a tree full of mangoes: P3 Science, Chapter 4, Life Cycles of Plants (pp. 76 to 79): how to observe a plant like a scientist, the three stages in the life cycle of a plant (the seed, the young plant and the adult plant), and why Singapore keeps a seed bank. Also fits US NGSS 3-LS1-1 (Grade 3: life cycles).
Safety: only an adult uses the knife. We never taste a plant we are studying. Weaver ants can bite: we look, and we do not touch.
Try it at home: plant a seed from a fruit you ate. Observe it every few days with your senses, measure it with a ruler from the soil, and write it down. Which comes out first, the root or the shoot?
Did you know? Singapore's first seed bank opened in 2019 at the Singapore Botanic Gardens. The Botanic Gardens also keeps a Herbarium of dried, pressed plants, started in 1875.
In the US, a Grade 3 class often grows a bean in a paper cup: the same three stages, seed, young plant and adult plant.
